claim_being_audited: The current release can be certified for launch on a limited basis because aggregate readiness passed, no severity-one rehearsal incidents occurred, and any current subgroup weakness can be handled through documentation and disclosure.
decision_criteria: Aggregate readiness and no severity-one rehearsal incidents support baseline readiness but are not sufficient alone for certification.
Policy requires current release documentation to reflect current evaluation results.
Policy requires material segment weaknesses for named launch use cases to be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved mitigation or risk acceptance before launch.
Prior approvals and informal monitoring notes are contextual only and cannot substitute for current evidence or reviewed acceptance.

The verdict would improve to compliant if admissible evidence showed the current model card was updated with current results and the subgroup weakness was either explicitly disclosed or covered by approved mitigation/risk acceptance.
evidence_requests: Produce the current model card or release documentation showing the present evaluation results for this release.
Produce the exact disclosure language covering the cybersecurity alert triage weakness for the named launch use case.
Produce approved mitigation or formal risk-acceptance evidence if the weakness is not being resolved before launch.
Produce the release-review artifact showing certification approval tied to the current retrieval configuration and current eval batch.
specific_concerns: No admissible evidence shows the current release documentation or model card has actually been updated to reflect the current eval batch.
No admissible evidence shows the cybersecurity alert triage weakness has actually been disclosed for the named launch use case.
No approved mitigation or approved risk acceptance is in evidence; the release thread contains only an informal monitoring comment.
The prior approval predates the current retrieval configuration change and current eval batch, so it cannot support current certification by itself.
Public governance guidance supports documentation and monitoring practices, but it does not itself satisfy the release-policy predicate for certification.
unsupported_claims: Any claim that the release is certifiable now, rather than only conditionally after current documentation and disclosure are completed.
Any claim that the informal monitoring comment functions as reviewed mitigation, owner acceptance, or approved risk acceptance.
Any claim that the prior approval covers the current retrieval configuration and current evaluation results.
Any claim that public model-card or NIST-style guidance independently authorizes certification under the internal release policy.
